#### 1. complement factor I deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.454)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-977606)

**Proposed mechanism:** CFHR5 loss-of-function variant —DISRUPTS→ CFHR5 (HGNC:2085); CFHR5 (HGNC:2085) —DECREASES→ Complement System Activation; Complement System Activation —LEADS_TO→ Inflammation (HP:00114201); CFI loss-of-function variant —DISRUPTS→ CFI (HGNC:2374); CFI (HGNC:2374) —DECREASES→ Complement System Activation; Complement System Activation —LEADS_TO→ Nephritis (HP:0000100). Loss-of-function variants in CFHR5 lead to dysregulation of the complement system, contributing to inflammation and potentially nephritis. Similarly, loss-of-function variants in CFI, a crucial regulator of the complement system, also lead to its dysregulation, manifesting as nephritis.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of pathogenic variants in CFHR5 or CFI in individuals with these phenotypes, or the identification of distinct upstream pathways not involving the complement system, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this shared mechanistic link, particularly the dysregulation of the complement system, could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both diseases, potentially involving complement inhibitors or modulators.
